# Rays Lisp

A `.rays` file declares a workspace with named graphs. Graphs evaluate immutable values; the native editor projects those same forms into editable graphs.

```sh
rays doc draw/circle
rays doc sop/
rays check --json sketches/basic.rays
rays render sketches/basic.rays -o basic.png --frame 30
rays fmt sketches/basic.rays
```

`doc` accepts an exact name, namespace prefix, or search word. `--json` exposes the registry; `--all` includes internal aliases. `check --json` writes one object per diagnostic. Commands exit 0 on success, 1 for diagnostics, and 2 for a crash. Rendering uses an offscreen GPU canvas and a fixed 60 Hz clock; `--size WIDTHxHEIGHT` and `--graph NAME` select the output.

## Workspace

```lisp
(workspace basic
  (graph picture
    (draw/circle [320 180] 42.5 :fill "#5aaaf0")))
```

A graph may omit `:context` when its body identifies one context. Explicit contexts remain legal. One draw graph without an editor graph opens as a canvas. `(ref name)` reads a graph; typed inputs use `(name : type)`. `let` and `let*` bind sequentially. Use `rays doc NAME` for the exact parameter types, defaults, ranges and units.

## Values and coercions

Integers, floats, booleans, text, vectors, lists, arrays, records and functions are values. A keyword begins with `:`. Strings use double quotes. `;` begins a line comment.

- Int widens to Float. Float does not round into Int; convert explicitly.
- A two-coordinate vector widens to vec3 with z = 0. Draw positions use logical points.
- A homogeneous list widens to the corresponding typed array.
- Draw radii and line widths accept fractional values. Angles are radians.
- Literal colours and choices are validated during checking.
- `=`, `/`, `nth` and `count` are the public polymorphic forms.
- Names use snake_case; axis suffixes come last, such as `divisions_x`.

## Forms

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `assoc` | Return a record with updated fields. |
| `case` | Match a value against literal alternatives. |
| `concat` | Join collections with a common element type. |
| `cond` | Select the result of the first true condition. |
| `defmacro` | Expand syntax before checking the workspace. |
| `defn` | Define a reusable function with typed inputs. |
| `defnode` | Define a reusable node with editable parameter metadata. |
| `error_rows` | Expose deferred diagnostics as data rows. |
| `filter` | Keep elements for which a predicate returns true. |
| `fn` | Create a pure anonymous function. |
| `fold` | Accumulate a result over a bounded collection. |
| `for` | Collect a result for each item in a bounded collection. |
| `get` | Read a field from a record. |
| `graph` | Declare a named, reactive graph. |
| `if` | Choose one of two values using a boolean condition. |
| `iterate` | Apply a pure function repeatedly with a fixed maximum count. |
| `let` | Bind names sequentially; later bindings can use earlier ones. |
| `list` | Construct a homogeneous list. |
| `map` | Apply a pure function to corresponding collection elements. |
| `quasiquote` | Build macro syntax with unquoted substitutions. |
| `quote` | Return syntax without evaluating it. |
| `reduce` | Reduce a collection into one accumulator value. |
| `ref` | Read another graph with optional input overrides. |
| `scan` | Collect intermediate accumulator values. |
| `sort_by` | Sort a collection by a numeric key. |
| `state` | Retain a value between frames and compute its next value. |
| `str` | Format and concatenate values as text. |
| `sum` | Add the numeric results of a bounded iteration. |
| `unquote` | Insert evaluated syntax inside quasiquote. |
| `unquote-splicing` | Insert a sequence of syntax forms inside quasiquote. |
| `values` | Return multiple named outputs from a node. |
| `with_error` | Map a runtime diagnostic to a recovery value. |
| `workspace` | Group graphs and reusable definitions into a workspace. |

The checked examples in `sketches/` cover larger workspaces. [Flow](../specification/flow.md) specifies language and editing contracts; [Rust crate map](../specification/api.md) explains extension ownership; [development](development.md) lists bounded checks and qualification.
